entries.title: Man critically wounded in shooting at Humboldt Park business
entries.summary: <p>A man was left in critical condition after a Humboldt Park shooting Friday evening. </p><p>A 31-year-old man was inside a business in the 4400 block of West Cortez Street at about 7:20 p.m. when he was approached and then shot by an "unknown offender," police said. </p><p>The man was hit in the chest and taken to Mount Sinai Hospital, reportedly in critical condition. </p><p>A person of interest in the case was taken into questioning, and a handgun was found at the scene, police said. </p><p>Area detectives are investigating. </p>

entries.title: Mayor Johnson, Trump, Obama remember football 'titan' Mike Ditka
entries.summary: <p>Hours before the Willis Towers’ antennas were set to light up in Bears blue and orange to honor Mike Ditka, whose death was announced Friday morning, Mayor Brandon Johnson acknowledged Ditka’s family, the city and “all who love Iron Mike.”</p><p>“Today, we lost a titan of the game and a hero of Chicago,” Johnson wrote in a statement on social media. “Mike Ditka revolutionized football and delivered glory to our great city on and off the field.”</p><p>He was among the dozens of political officials taking to social media to celebrate Ditka’s life.</p><p>Former President Barack Obama posted his own message on X with a photo of himself and Ditka holding up a Bears jersey emblazoned with Obama and the number 85 during a 2011 ceremony honoring the 1985 Super Bowl team at the White House. </p><p>The team’s original trip to the White House to meet Ronald Reagan had been scrapped following the explosion of the Challenger space shuttle that year.</p><p>Obama said that when he arrived in Chicago in 1985, Ditka and the championship team “were king.” It was high praise from a man Ditka once called the “<a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/2016/3/4/18409790/could-ditka-s-rant-against-obama-end-his-espn-deal" target="_blank" ><u>worst president we’ve ever had</u></a>” while voicing his support for President Donald Trump and former president Ronald Reagan.</p><p>“Coach Ditka set the tone for a team that was punishing, dominant, and fun — and the city loved him for it,” Obama wrote on social media. “I'm thinking of the Ditka family and Bears fans everywhere on the passing of a legend.”</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">When I got to Chicago in the summer of 1985, Mike Ditka and the Chicago Bears were king. Coach Ditka set the tone for a team that was punishing, dominant, and fun — and the city loved him for it. I'm thinking of the Ditka family and Bears fans everywhere on the passing of a… <a href="https://t.co/RKlJsahYbR">pic.twitter.com/RKlJsahYbR</a></p>— Barack Obama (@BarackObama) <a href="https://x.com/BarackObama/status/2108641562431197517?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">October 9, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p>Trump, who was informed of Ditka’s passing during a news briefing Friday, said the late coach was “great” while touting his support while he was alive.</p><p>"He was a great guy,” Trump told reporters. “He was with me all the way. He was tough. That's a sad one.”</p><p>Illinois officials posted their own tributes to “da coach,” as U.S. Sen. Dick Durbin called him in his message. Durbin, who <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/politics/senator-dick-durbin-reelection" target="_blank" >announced last </a>year that he would step down after five terms in the U.S. Senate and seven terms in the U.S. House, said Ditka coached with “style, grace, and respect for the game.”</p><p>“No Bears fan will ever forget the day when the Monsters of the Midway triumphed over the New England Patriots in Super Bowl XX,” Durbin said in a social media post. “Loretta and I will be praying for his family, friends, and former players as well as the millions of Chicagoans and Bears fans in mourning.”</p><p>Gov. JB Pritzker wrote on social media that "Da Coach was not only an icon in Chicago, but the entire football world. Our thoughts are with Mike Ditka’s family, friends, and Bears fans today. May his memory be a blessing."</p><p>“Few people are as synonymous with Chicago as Mike Ditka,” Sen. Tammy Duckworth said in her own statement on social media. “Illinois will miss him dearly, but his legacy will never be forgotten. My heart goes out to his family and everyone who loved Da Coach.”</p><p>Longtime political consultant and former Obama advisor David Axelrod also expressed condolences for Ditka while sharing a story of filming a political campaign ad with him for former Chicago Mayor Richard M. Daley.</p><p>“When he popped in to do the spot, I started to explain what we were going for,” Axelrod wrote. “He looked at me with a withering stare and said, ‘Just turn on the F-ing camera. I know what I want to say.’ He always did.”</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/obituaries/2026/10/09/mike-ditka-dead-bears-coach" >Mike Ditka, who coached the Bears to their only Super Bowl championship, has died</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/09/bears-fans-mourn-mike-ditka-the-man-who-unified-city-sports-fans-and-taught-chicago-to-hate-green-bay" >Bears fans mourn Mike Ditka, the man who unified city sports fans and ‘taught Chicago to hate Green Bay’</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/09/da-coach-mike-ditka-embodied-chicago-city-he-adopted" >‘Da Coach’ Mike Ditka embodied Chicago, the city he adopted</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p></p>

entries.title: Blackhawks' Frank Nazar suspended two games for hit on Islanders' Bo Horvat
entries.summary: <p>Blackhawks forward Frank Nazar received a two-game suspension Friday, marking the first time a Hawks player has been suspended since 2021. </p><p>Nazar got the news Friday after a phone hearing with the NHL's department of player safety regarding his check to Bo Horvat's head in the final minutes of the Hawks-Islanders game Thursday.</p><p>Horvat was in the process of nailing the Hawks' empty net from long range — and did have his head down and out — when Nazar gave it a direct blow while skating by. </p><p>The hit incited a brawl, and Islanders coach Pete DeBoer later said Horvat was being evaluated for injury. Nazar received a match penalty, which was inconsequential with the game out of reach and about to end.</p><p>The suspension, which will sideline him Saturday against the Hurricanes and Tuesday against the Penguins, poses a much bigger problem for the Hawks.</p><p>He'll join injured veterans Teuvo Teravainen and Andrew Mangiapane on their list of unavailable forwards, likely prompting another AHL call-up.</p><p>Nazar, who has three points in five games this season, will also forfeit over $68,000 in salary due to the suspension.</p><p>He's the first Hawk to get suspended since former forward Brett Connolly received a four-game ban for interference on former Stars forward Tanner Kero — who was stretchered off after the incident — in December 2021.</p>
entries.author: Ben Pope

entries.title: Mike Ditka inspired comedic gold. But the funniest riff was Ditka as Ditka.
entries.summary: <p>Mike Ditka could bowl over a linebacker, make a sensational catch, motivate his players to greatness, dress down a reporter, out-heckle a heckler, sell you a refrigerator, coach “The Refrigerator,” and make an entire city laugh without ever telling a joke.</p><p>And then he’d have a cigar.</p><p>While Mike Ditka’s primary and iconic legacy as a football player and coach is celebrated elsewhere on these pages, let’s also give Ditka his due as a personality and a performer who starred in dozens of local and national commercials, appeared on “Saturday Night Live” and “Cheers,” and proved to be a worthy comedic partner to Will Ferrell on the big screen.</p><p>This list of football greats turned actors is extensive and impressive, from Jim Brown and Alex Karras to Don Meredith to Merlin Olsen, from Dick Butkus to Fred Dryer, from Terry Bradshaw to Peyton Manning to Nnamdi Asomugha. But whereas we could buy into Jim Brown playing Robert Jefferson in “The Dirty Dozen,” or Fred Dryer as “Hunter” and Merlin Olsen as “Father Murphy,” or even Peyton Manning as Coach Gary on “Modern Family,” Ditka almost always played <i>Ditka</i>.</p><p>On rare occasions, Ditka portrayed a fictional character — for example, “Coach Mafferty” on a couple of episodes of “3rd Rock from the Sun” in 1997, and the mayor of Chicago in a Make-A-Wish Foundation short film project called “Madzilla!” in 2014 — but from episodes of “L.A. Law,” “Coach,” “Becker” and “Entourage,” among other series, the coach played a lightly fictionalized version of himself, and invariably stole the scene.</p><p>It made sense. Ditka was just going to swallow any character whole anyway. How could you script somebody more alpha, more intense, more intimidating, more complicated, more hilarious and more memorable than the real Mike Ditka?</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Provided</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>The coach was a Hall of Fame presence in TV ads, from local spots for rustproofers and car dealerships to national spots for products too numerous to mention, including a memorable Super Bowl ad when he donned Packers gear and Jerry Rice wore Cowboys merch. (One of my favorites: the 1988 “Calling Me Home, Chicago” tourism ad, with Butkus returning home and surprising Ditka at Butch McGuire’s, and the two exchange the simplest and most profound greetings: “Butkus.” “Ditka.” Pure gold.)</p><p>Unscripted Ditka was also magnificently unpredictable, whether he was heckling back at hecklers at press conferences or on sports talk radio, donning roller skates and barreling through the Bears’ offices after dubbing Minnesota’s old indoor arena “The Rollerdome,” or racing through “Take Me Out to the Ballgame” at Wrigley Field in a land-speed record of 22 seconds in 1998.</p><p>The most complete meta-Ditka performance came in the 2005 comedy “Kicking and Screaming,” in which Will Ferrell’s quintessential suburban dad, Phil Weston, recruits Ditka to be the assistant coach for Phil’s son’s youth soccer team. It’s a fully realized role, with Ditka leaning into his hot-tempered persona to mine tremendous laughs. (In our two thumbs up review of the film on “Ebert & Roeper,” I said Ditka deserved a sitcom deal based on this performance; Roger noted, “Ditka is playing himself, and playing himself as nobody else could, and he gets laughs out of just turning and looking at Will Ferrell.”)</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="HtmlModule"><a class="AnchorLink" id="html-embed-module-d10000" name="html-embed-module-d10000"></a><iframe width="560" height="315" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/B9NO24hbe8Q?si=UwX-y2oKeB5WI5YT" title="YouTube video player" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen></iframe> </div> </div><p>On a personal note, I had the privilege of narrating a live reading of the unproduced “Superfans” movie script written by Robert Smigel and Bob Odenkirk, the creators of that legendary series of sketches. In an Instagram post on Friday, Smigel told the story of 2001 ESPN roast of Ditka where Ditka eschewed the traditional rebuttal: “The whole event was a benefit for Misericordia, a residence where … children and adults with intellectual disabilities are provided personalized care … Coach Ditka used his time to talk about … what Misericordia provides. He could’ve gotten huge laughs firing back at all of us but he cared much more about Misericordia.”</p><p>The live reading of “Da Bears Movie Dat Wasn’t” was staged at the Park West in June of 2010, with performers including Smigel, Odenkirk, George Wendt, Joe Mantegna, David Koechner, my Sun-Times colleague Rick Telander, Keith Van Horne and Ryan Dempster — but it was Dikta as Ditka who stole the show.</p><p>As he did every time.</p>

entries.title: Reopened probe into CPS Board president candidate’s alleged inappropriate contact with teen could end soon
entries.summary: <p>The Chicago Public Schools’ inspector general could soon issue findings in its recently reopened investigation into whether Hilario Dominguez, a candidate for Chicago School Board president, acted inappropriately with a 17-year-old in 2017.</p><p>Investigators interviewed the woman, who is now 26, in late September and reinterviewed Dominguez on Tuesday.</p><p>The woman <a class="Link" href="https://www.chicagotribune.com/2026/10/02/cps-watchdog-school-board-president-candidate/" target="_blank" ><u>told the Chicago Tribune</u></a> and other media outlets that Dominguez asked about her dating life while they were alone in a car, and he once lifted her up in a hug and spun her around. At the time, Dominguez was 24 and an organizer at The Resurrection Project, a Pilsen-based nonprofit, while she was a CPS student working there through the city’s summer jobs program.</p><p>The woman <a class="Link" href="https://www.chalkbeat.org/chicago/2026/10/07/chicago-public-schools-watchdog-reopens-inquiry-into-hilario-dominguez/" target="_blank" ><u>told Chalkbeat and Block Club Chicago</u></a> that the hug with her body pressed against his made her feel “very uncomfortable” and that the car interaction was “really alarming” because Dominguez “was a figure of authority that I trusted.” She also said the concerning behavior stopped after she complained to an adult staffer.</p><p>The young woman has personal ties to Dominguez’s former political rival, Aida Flores, according to several sources. Dominguez denies the allegations and says they are politically motivated.</p><p>“For me, this is beyond a political campaign,” he told WBEZ. “This is about how I hold my head up high in the neighborhoods and in the city that raised me.”</p><p>The school district’s watchdog first opened an investigation into the alleged incidents in 2021 when Dominguez was teaching in CPS. He left that position in 2022 to work as deputy political director for the Chicago Teachers Union, which endorsed Dominguez in the school board race.</p><p>Earlier this year, the inspector general’s office determined the allegations were unsubstantiated, according to an email sent by an investigator to Dominguez reviewed by WBEZ. But the office recently reopened the case.</p><p>Inspector General Philip Wagenknecht would not comment on why, but the woman<b> </b>told the Tribune that she reached out to his office because <a class="Link" href="https://www.chicagotribune.com/2026/10/06/school-board-candidates-contenders-conduct/" target="_blank" ><u>she was not interviewed for the original investigation</u></a>.</p><p>These accusations have been thrust into Chicago’s heated <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/graphics/chicago-school-board-education-voter-guide/school-board/president/" target="_blank" ><u>school board president contest</u></a>.</p><p>Jessica Biggs, one of Dominguez’s opponents in the race, said the alleged conduct was “deeply concerning” and that women and girls in CPS are paying attention.</p><p>“They deserve to know that the next leader of the CPS Board of Education will take their experiences seriously,” she said.</p><p>One of Biggs’ staffers, Alaina Hampton, said in a statement that she has known the woman for years and was long aware of the allegations. Hampton said the woman reached out to her in early September when the inspector general informed her the case was closed. Hampton recommended the woman hire a lawyer. Hampton said she would “continue to stand in solidarity with victims and survivors.”</p><p>Hampton was part of a high-profile sexual harassment lawsuit filed in 2018 against the Democratic Party of Illinois and others. <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/2019/11/29/20988763/alaina-hampton-federal-lawsuit-madigan-quinn-settlement" target="_blank" ><u>She settled that case</u></a>.</p><p>Through her lawyer, the woman declined to respond to questions from WBEZ. But she has said she is speaking out now because she wanted to tell her own story. <a class="Link" href="https://www.nbcchicago.com/video/local/inappropriate-behavior-alleged-against-school-board-president-candidate/3998741/" target="_blank" ><u>She told NBC Chicago</u></a> that Dominguez’s interactions with her should disqualify him from serving as school board president.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="Figure-content"><figcaption class="Figure-caption"><p>People gathered during a press conference outside The Resurrection Project in 2023. A woman alleges that Hilario Dominguez acted inappropriately with her when she worked at the Pilsen-based nonprofit through a summer jobs program in 2017.</p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Anthony Vazquez/Sun-Times file</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>Dominguez left the Resurrection Project in 2018 to run for alderperson of the 25th Ward. Flores, an assistant principal at CPS, was one of four opponents.</p><p>Dominguez says these allegations first surfaced during that race. They both lost.</p><p>When Flores ran a second time in 2023, she was backed by a political action committee that opposes the CTU. Flores’ campaign website says she’s collecting petitions to run again in February.</p><p>Flores said in an email to WBEZ that she would not discuss the matter while the inspector general’s investigation was ongoing. Earlier this week, Flores told Chalkbeat and Block Club that she was not involved in surfacing the allegations.</p><p>Dominguez insists “that he did not have those types of interactions” with the woman.</p><p>He also said that he believes sexual misconduct should be taken seriously.</p><p>Paloma Rodriguez, a former housing coordinator for The Resurrection Project, told WBEZ that she sent emails in 2017 telling senior management that the young woman felt uncomfortable around Dominguez.</p><p>When Dominguez announced he was running for office in 2018, she said she decided to become “louder” about the alleged behavior. She submitted an official report to senior management in December 2018, according to a redacted copy reviewed by WBEZ. Rodriguez told WBEZ she also wrote it to “cover her butt” and preserve the information.</p><p>Rodriguez wrote, in 2018, that the teen told her “there was inappropriate language and behavior” by Dominguez in 2017, including “questions and comments about her dating life and physical appearance.”</p><p>Salvador Cerna, who supervised Dominguez at The Resurrection Project and is now his father-in-law, told WBEZ he never “had to discipline Hilario” or discuss “his interactions with youth.”</p><p>A Resurrection Project spokeswoman said the organization would not comment.</p><p>Rodriguez, who said she was close friends with Flores but recently had a falling out, said she did not release the internal Resurrection Project report. She stands by her decision to report what the young woman told her.</p><p>“We really need to hold men specifically accountable,” Rodriguez said.</p><p>State Rep. Theresa Mah, who endorsed Dominguez in the 2019 City Council race, heard the allegations swirling around her Pilsen-area district. She told WBEZ that she talked to the executive director of The Resurrection Project, Raul Raymundo, in 2019 and was “satisfied that no misconduct occurred.”</p>

entries.title: 5th beluga whale dies at Shedd Aquarium
entries.summary: <p>Another beluga whale rescued from the Marineland of Canada has died, the Shedd Aquarium announced Friday.</p><p>Caspian is the fourth rescued beluga to die at the Chicago aquarium since their initial arrival in July, joining eight resident whales. A resident beluga at the Shedd, Beethoven, also died recently at 34, likely due to age-related issues, the aquarium said.</p><p>Five belugas rescued from the Canadian aquatic park have died in total, out of 30 rescued. One taken in by <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/2026/09/18/3rd-beluga-dies-marineland-canada-shedd-aquarium" target="_blank" ><u>Oceanografic Valencia in Spain</u></a>, died last month.</p><p>The succession of deaths in less than three months has made it clear that the rescued whales were “made vulnerable by chronic and severe illness,” Shedd spokesperson Johnny Ford told the Chicago Sun-Times.</p><p>Limited diagnostic information available about the rescued belugas made it difficult to determine which were most at risk, Ford said.</p><p>Caspian’s condition “crashed” earlier this week, the aquarium said, and she was kept on life support for nearly four hours in an attempt to save her.</p><p>The deterioration of Caspian and the aquarium's “intensive efforts” to save her deepen the mystery of what ailed the animal. Blood samples examined this week showed abnormalities in both her electrolyte levels and blood pH, according to a statement from the Shedd.</p><p>Her blood pH showed it had become "dangerously acidic," revealing a clearer picture of how sick she was, the statement said. But the information doesn’t help determine what led to her death.</p><p>“Caspian’s loss is felt deeply by the people who knew and cared for her and by those who followed her story,” the statement said. “Our team worked to give her every opportunity to recover. We will share what her examination adds to our understanding with the same care and openness.”</p><p>Peekachu, a 23-year-old female, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/museums-zoos/2026/08/26/one-of-the-shedds-rescued-beluga-whales-has-died" target="_blank" ><u>died Aug. 25</u></a>, and Rain, a 20-year-old female, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/museums-zoos/2026/09/03/shedd-aquarium-beluga" target="_blank" ><u>died Sept. 2</u></a>. Osiris, a 26-year-old female, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/museums-zoos/2026/09/21/3rd-beluga-whale-dies-shedd-aquarium-moved-marineland-canada-niagara-falls" target="_blank" ><u>died Sept. 2</u></a>1. The rescued beluga in Spain, Jelly Bean, died Sept. 18.</p><p>Reports conducted so far on the other whales showed they had preexisting, chronic conditions.</p><p>Final reports on the deaths of Peekachu and Rain showed major chronic inflammation in their digestive systems, among other issues like hypertension, liver tissue death and lung scarring.</p><p>Experts said these conditions could have elevated their risk of cardiovascular stress, according to the Shedd’s statement.</p><p>Preliminary investigations into the death of Osiris identified chronic liver disease, but her report is unfinished.</p><p>Animal rights activists in the United States and Canada have questioned whether the belugas were healthy enough to endure the stress of being transferred out of Marineland — in trucks and then airplanes.</p><p>"Five dead belugas tells us that after years of neglect at Marineland, these whales were not healthy enough to withstand the stress of transport,” said Camille Labchuk, executive director of Animal Justice, a Toronto, Canada-based animal rights advocacy group. "It's heartbreaking that Marineland was allowed to rush through this transfer operation to clear the way for its lucrative land deal. Marineland had years to plan for their retirement to a sanctuary, but failed to do so. Now, the whales are paying the price."</p><p>The rescued belugas were allegedly living in poor conditions at the shuttered aquatic park in Canada, just south of Niagara Falls.</p><p>Shedd is part of a consortium of four U.S. aquariums, as well as Oceanografic in Spain, that together agreed to take the belugas languishing in Marineland. The park closed to the public in 2024, citing financial troubles.</p>
